Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
3:41 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because paying someone now takes a few seconds and costs almost nothing.

Not long ago, you needed cash, a card machine, or a bank transfer with long account details. Now you scan a QR code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves straight from your bank account. It works the same way at a roadside chai stall and at a big shopping mall. Since nearly everyone has a smartphone and a bank account, more people try it, and the more people use it, the more shops accept it.

Three reasons stand out:

Speed and ease: Payments take seconds, work any hour of any day including holidays, and need no change.
Low or no cost: Sending money to people is free, and most shops pay no fee. Small sellers keep what they earn instead of losing a cut to card charges.
Works everywhere: One app can link several banks, and almost every seller, from vegetable carts to malls, shows a QR code.

There is also a quiet bonus: every payment leaves a record on your phone, so tracking spending gets easier. Trust has grown too, because people see friends, family and local shopkeepers using it daily without trouble.
